A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe OpticalRS-13M and SelectiveMAE. Their complete main texts and appendices, including tables, figures, equations, and algorithms, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original pre-training, downstream classification, detection, segmentation, efficiency, and ablation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v5 retains original experimental results and reports additional selector, similarity-measure, scaling, and CrossMAE comparisons. Its disclosure that some baseline scores come from other papers does not negate its original results.

M1.justification: The HOG-based partial reconstruction, cross-attention decoder, and progressive semantic token selection procedure remain unchanged. Equations (1)-(6), Algorithm 1, and the default masking and reconstruction ratios describe the same method. New selector alternatives are ablations.

E1.justification: Both versions use MillionAID and OpticalRS-13M for pre-training and retain AID, RESISC-45, DIOR, DIOR-R, LoveDA, and SpaceNetv1 evaluation. Naming and describing OpticalRS-4M does not establish new represented coverage beyond the existing optical-image subsets.

E2.justification: v5 adds an evaluated CrossMAE comparison in Table 6 and a pretrained Swin-B selector in Table 2. LSKNet disappears from the main benchmark table, and Figure 1 replaces RVSA with CrossMAE, although RVSA remains in the main table. AdaMAE/ATS was already evaluated in v4's appendix.

E3.justification: The efficiency comparison changes its stated setting from MillionAID with 1,600 epochs (v4 Table 3) to OpticalRS-13M subsets with 800 epochs (v5 Table 5). The epoch study shifts from four-million-image training to thirteen-million-image training, alongside additional 800-epoch selector and similarity experiments. These substantially revise the experimental design, while the default configurations, downstream splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v5 adds tests of learned alternatives to HOG and Euclidean/Manhattan alternatives to cosine distance. It extends the fixed-throughput analysis to SelectiveMAE and reworks the epoch-sensitivity study, but removes the controlled detection and segmentation results from v4's dataset-diversity analysis. Existing appendix reconstruction, decoder-depth, masking-ratio, and selection-order ablations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run statistics, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Results continue to be presented as point estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous retained results change: full-data SelectiveMAE ViT-B RESISC-45 accuracy changes from 92.53/94.50 to 93.70/95.48, and DIOR mAP50 from 75.10 to 75.80 (v4 Table 5; v5 Table 1). Four-million-image MAE AID accuracy changes from 96.88/98.22 to 96.58/98.02. v5 also adds ablation, CrossMAE, and epoch-study results while removing dataset-scaling detection and segmentation entries. Revised timing results accompany changed experimental settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning in Equations (1)-(6) are retained. Equation (3) receives equivalent notation and typesetting changes; neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a large, diverse optical RS dataset and efficient SelectiveMAE pre-training. Claims of improved downstream representations, over twofold acceleration, and sufficient training using 40% of image patches remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations favoring HOG's speed over the slightly more accurate Swin-B selector and describing limited sensitivity to distance choice. It drops v4 Section 6.2's qualification about diminishing returns from longer training. The substantive limitations and societal-impact discussion in Section 6.7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds a linked planned release of the dataset, code, and trained models; exact image/pixel counts and satellite-source information; and explicit t-SNE and eight-A100 measurement details. It also identifies the sources of borrowed baseline scores and describes the new selector implementations. Table 9's default configurations remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for t-SNE, RomA, satellite platforms, ResNet, and Swin, and removes LSKNet. The CrossMAE discussion expands around the shared decoder and direct comparison. The broader positioning around dataset scale, diversity, and efficient remote-sensing pre-training remains stable.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative now presents main results before ablations. Dataset-collection and preprocessing procedures move from Section 3.1 to appendix Section 6.2, replacing its former extended-training discussion. The title, author block, contribution list, and several introductory and experimental passages are also revised.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and a new Figure 3 compares dataset volumes and image modalities. Experimental tables are substantially reorganized: the main comparison gains throughput, timing tables are consolidated, and the dataset study loses detection/segmentation columns while gaining new sections. Appendix visual examples remain the same apart from numbering and placement.

improvement.justification: The new HOG and similarity ablations and direct CrossMAE comparison strengthen method validation, while added access and provenance details improve documentation. However, v5 removes v4's controlled detection/segmentation evidence for dataset benefits. Its new CrossMAE table also specifies 400 million sampled images, leaving its relationship to the four-million-image comparisons unclear. These gains and losses in evidential strength prevent a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
